title: SLI vs SLO vs SLA
subtitle: Turn reliability expectations into measurable targets
learning_objective: Distinguish a service indicator, internal objective, and external agreement.

scenes.title: IS THE SERVICE RELIABLE?
scenes.body: “It feels slow” is hard to act on. A clear reliability target gives teams a measurable signal.

scenes.title: Three related terms
scenes.body: An SLI is the measured indicator, such as successful request ratio. An SLO is the target for that indicator. An SLA is an agreement that may include consequences if targets are missed.

scenes.title: Pick a user-facing signal
scenes.body: Choose indicators users care about—availability, latency, or correctness—and define the measurement window and eligible requests.

scenes.question: Which term describes the target a team aims to meet?
scenes.explanation: The SLO sets a target for an indicator. An SLA is an external agreement and may include remedies.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Measure with an SLI, set a target with an SLO, and understand any external SLA separately.
